RequiredPredicateError.description: A RequiredPredicateError occurs when a cryptographic object does not satisfy a required security condition. CrySL rules may specify that a cryptographic object must fulfill a security property (e.g., a key must be generated securely before use). If this property is missing or unverified, this error is reported. Such errors indicate that the cryptographic operation might not meet the required security guarantees, leading to potential vulnerabilities such as weak key material or improper algorithm usage.

A RequiredPredicateError was triggered because one or more required conditions were not fulfilled before using java.security.KeyPair.

According to the CrySL rule, the following predicates must hold:
  • generatedPrivkey[privateKey] — the private key must be generated securely
  • generatedPubkey[publicKey] — the public key must be generated securely
  • If KeyPair is not constructed in the current code (i.e., no call to new KeyPair(...)), then it must be a valid, generated key pair from a cryptographic API: generatedKeypair[this, _]

This error indicates that you're either using keys that weren't generated properly, or using a KeyPair instance without verifying its origin.

A RequiredPredicateError was detected, indicating that a necessary precondition (predicate) for using KeyPairGenerator was not fulfilled.

This error happens when the AlgorithmParameterSpec provided during initialize() has not been prepared correctly for the specified algorithm. The CrySL rule requires different kinds of prepared parameter specs based on the algorithm:
  • RSA -> preparedRSA[params]
  • DSA -> preparedDSA[params]
  • DiffieHellman or DH -> preparedDH[params]
  • EC -> preparedEC[params]

If the params object passed to initialize() is not properly constructed, this predicate fails, resulting in the error.

A RequiredPredicateError occurred because the PrivateKey object was used without being verified as a securely generated key.

The CrySL rule for java.security.PrivateKey requires that the predicate generatedPrivkey[this] be satisfied before using methods like getEncoded(). This means the private key must originate from a trusted and cryptographically secure source.

Using hardcoded keys, deserialized keys from untrusted sources, or keys created without proper generation can lead to this violation and may introduce severe security vulnerabilities.

A RequiredPredicateError occurred in the use of the java.security.Signature API due to missing required predicates defined in the CrySL rule.

This error indicates that the key material used during initialization was not securely generated or verified. The following conditions must be satisfied before using the Signature API:
  • If initSign(privateKey) or initSign(privateKey, random) is used -> generatedPrivkey[privateKey] must hold
  • If initVerify(publicKey) or initVerify(certificate) is used -> generatedPubkey[publicKey] must hold
Failing to establish these predicates can lead to insecure or incorrect use of the Signature API.
